paper_metadata.title: A framework to evaluate the performance of Variational Quantum Algorithms

summary: The paper proposes a benchmarking framework for Variational Quantum Algorithms solving QUBO problems using three metrics—feasibility, quality, and reproducibility—evaluated via 400 repeated optimizations per configuration. A proof‑of‑concept simulation on a 16‑qubit random QUBO instance tests CVaR cost functions (α ∈ {0.15–1.0}) and shot counts from 1,000 to 100,000, identifying several configurations (e.g., α = 0.75 with ≥10,000 shots) that pass feasibility (≥0.70), quality (≥1.20), and reproducibility (≥0.60) thresholds.

experiments.description: Simulation-based benchmarking of multiple variational quantum algorithms on a fixed 16-qubit QUBO instance using a RealAmplitudes ansatz, CVaR cost functions, and COBYLA optimization, evaluated across varying shot counts and CVaR parameters.

algorithm.variant: Generic VQA benchmarking (RealAmplitudes ansatz + CVaR objective)
algorithm.ansatz: RealAmplitudes with reverse-linear entanglement and one repetition
algorithm.parameter_initialization: same randomly chosen initial quantum circuit for all optimizations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 16 binary variables mapped to 16 qubits; gate-based variational circuit used to sample bitstrings for the QUBO objective
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize f(x)=x^T Q x over x in {0,1}^N

problem_instance.description: Fixed random QUBO instance of dimension 16

dataset_specification.description: random QUBO instance; available upon reasonable request

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 400 independent optimizations per VQA instance; feasibility, quality, and reproducibility estimated with 95% confidence intervals across repeated runs

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute feasibility, quality, and reproducibility from repeated optimization outcomes; discretize quality diagram into 0.1 x 0.1 bins for entropy-based reproducibility

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline or speedup claim is reported; the paper is a benchmarking framework study on simulated VQAs.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; the work evaluates benchmarking metrics (feasibility, quality, reproducibility) for VQAs on a 16‑qubit QUBO instance rather than scaling performance against classical algorithms.
limiting_factors: Only a single 16‑qubit QUBO instance evaluated
No comparison with classical optimization algorithms
Experiments performed only in noiseless simulation
Framework evaluates benchmarking metrics rather than computational speed or solution quality vs classical methods
No asymptotic complexity or scaling analysis

notes: Paper explicitly states a 16-qubit QUBO instance and use of Qiskit with variational quantum circuits; no specific QPU is named, so hardware is treated as simulation-based.
The paper reports the RealAmplitudes ansatz with one repetition and 32 parameters, but does not report circuit depth, transpiled depth, or gate counts.
The study is benchmarking methodology-focused and does not provide asymptotic quantum/classical complexity or a speedup claim.
The paper does not claim quantum advantage; its focus is on defining evaluation metrics for VQAs.
No classical baselines or scaling comparisons are reported, making advantage assessment impossible.
